title: Pinostrobin attenuates microglia-mediated neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage through modulation of the MYC-CTSL signaling axis.
authors: Liu, Qi; Wang, Yihan; Wang, Bingchuan; Yang, Dujiang; Wang, Jinyu; Ou, Wenxin; Tang, Qiang; Zhou, Wei; Zhang, Mingwei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮类化合物pinostrobin通过MYC-CTSL轴减轻蛛网膜下腔出血后神经炎症，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且MYC/CTSL非TF-DNA结合体系，仅方法部分可借鉴。
abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is a life-threatening neurological emergency associated with high mortality and poor functional outcomes. Early brain injury (EBI) within the first 72 h critically influences prognosis, with excessive microglial activation representing a key contributor to neuroinflammation and secondary neuronal damage. Identifying pharmacological agents capable of modulating microglia-driven inflammatory responses remains an important therapeutic challenge. In this study, we investigated the potential anti-inflammatory mechanisms of pinostrobin (PIN), a natural flavonoid with reported neuroprotective properties. By integrating bioinformatics, network pharmacology, and machine learning approaches (LASSO, random forest, and SVM), MYC and CTSL were identified as candidate targets potentially linking PIN to SAH-related inflammatory pathways. Molecular docking and 50-ns molecular dynamics simulations suggested stable interactions between PIN and these proteins. Furthermore, in vitro evidence from LPS-stimulated BV2 microglial cells demonstrated that PIN reduced the expression of MYC, CTSL, NF-kappaB p65, and IL-1beta, accompanied by attenuation of microglial inflammatory activation. Collectively, these findings suggest that PIN may modulate neuroinflammatory cascades relevant to EBI after SAH, potentially through regulation of the MYC-CTSL axis. This study provides integrative, hypothesis-generating insights into the microglia-targeted anti-inflammatory potential of PIN in the context of SAH.
abstract_zh: 蛛网膜下腔出血（SAH）是一种危及生命的神经科急症，与高死亡率和不良功能结局相关。发病后72小时内的早期脑损伤（EBI）对预后具有关键影响，其中小胶质细胞过度激活是神经炎症和继发性神经元损伤的重要促成因素。识别能够调节小胶质细胞驱动的炎症反应的药物制剂仍是重要的治疗挑战。在本研究中，我们探讨了松属素（PIN）——一种具有报道的神经保护特性的天然黄酮类化合物——的潜在抗炎机制。通过整合生物信息学、网络药理学和机器学习方法（LASSO、随机森林和SVM），MYC和CTSL被确定为可能将PIN与SAH相关炎症通路联系起来的候选靶点。分子对接和50纳秒分子动力学模拟表明PIN与这些蛋白质之间存在稳定相互作用。此外，来自LPS刺激的BV2小胶质细胞的体外证据表明，PIN降低了MYC、CTSL、NF-kappaB p65和IL-1beta的表达，并伴随小胶质细胞炎症激活的减弱。总体而言，这些发现提示PIN可能通过调节MYC-CTSL轴，调节与SAH后EBI相关的神经炎症级联反应。本研究为PIN在SAH背景下靶向小胶质细胞的抗炎潜力提供了整合性、假设生成的见解。
